metadata.title: Taipei dbt companies and people for the Taipei dbt Meetup
metadata.purpose: Find Taipei companies using dbt, and people who could speak at or attend the Taipei dbt Meetup.
method: v1 (2026-10-01): v1 (2026-10-01): one research sub-agent. Only 3 web searches ran before the session's search cap was reached, so the run used direct fetches: iThome 鐵人賽 site search and the dbt tag (about 300 articles read for author and series), the chapter's Medium publication via a reader proxy, Meetup GraphQL for R-Ladies Taipei, Taipei Women in Tech, PyData Taipei, GDG Taipei and the chapter, KKTIX listings for DevOps Taiwan, COSCUP 2024-25 session JSON, the Recce blog, GitHub user search and the dbt-local-taipei org. Past chapter speakers added from enriched/taipei-dbt-meetup.json. Same scoring rules as berlin_planning/SEARCH_METHOD.md §1 Step 6.
Lesson: iThome 鐵人賽 is the richest source of emerging voices in Taiwan; article pages give the author handle, series and date, and curl with a browser user agent works where WebFetch gets 403.
Lesson: the iThome dbt tag mostly returns the chapter's own 2023-24 writing teams, so most dbt authors there are already past speakers; data-engineering search terms find the new names.
Lesson: Medium, Yourator job pages, Cake and 104 are behind Cloudflare; a reader proxy (r.jina.ai) reads Medium posts but not job ads.
Lesson: Meetup GraphQL groupSearch around Taipei's coordinates lists the local data groups; R-Ladies Taipei is the one active women-in-data community with speaker bios.
Lesson: KKTIX organiser feeds (<org>.kktix.cc/events.json) list DevOps Taiwan events, including the panel co-hosted with the chapter, with names and employers.

v1 (2026-10-01): location pass. 24 people placed from public pages (Meetup hosts and RSVPs, GitHub, speaker bios, author boxes, recent in-person talks at a local-office employer) and LinkedIn search results (1 of them),, or from the same person's located record in another chapter's file, by the evidence rules in research/README.md. Each placed person has a 'location (high|medium)' note and evidence link. 44 people are still unknown.

v2 (2026-10-01): women-in-data pass with fetches only (no web search, about 15 fetches): Meetup gql2 groupSearch near Taipei with 18 queries; WiDS site search; the WiDS Taipei 2024, 2025 and 2026 conference pages and its Medium feed; the GDG Taipei events API and the WTM Taipei Design x Data event; PyLadies Taiwan on KKTIX; Girls in Tech Taiwan. 18 people added (9 speakers and 9 organisers as connectors), plus WiDS talks for 3 people and WTM Taipei talks for 2 past chapter speakers already in the file. Nobody's gender is recorded or inferred; no pronouns were self-published.

Lesson: WiDS Taipei (widstaipei.org) is the main women-in-data event in Taiwan. The conference pages name speakers and organisers but not talk titles; the Medium feed (medium.com/feed/women-in-data-science-taipei) has a write-up of each talk with the speaker's bio, and reads with a plain fetch.
Lesson: WTM Taipei runs through GDG Taipei (gdg.community.dev chapter 748). Its 2024-25 events are career workshops; event details sit in the events API, so no page fetch is needed.
Lesson: PyLadies Taiwan's KKTIX feed has had no event since 2014.

v3 (2026-10-01): company pass with fetches only (no web search, about 15 fetches): the freehire.me open API (skills=dbt, countries=TW, 3 ads), Greenhouse, Lever and Ashby boards for about 55 employers with Taipei offices, the Yourator search API, the 104 job bank API, Meetup gql2 group search near Taipei plus the past events of the chapter and Grafana & Friends Taipei, Hacker News Who is hiring through Algolia (2 queries), and GitHub code search for dbt_project.yml in 9 Taiwanese company organisations.
Lesson: the freehire.me JSON API finds only 3 Taiwanese ads tagged dbt; Taiwanese employers mostly use 104, Cake and Yourator, which block plain fetches.
Lesson: the 104 job bank API (www.104.com.tw/jobs/search/api/jobs) returns a Cloudflare challenge to a plain fetch.
Lesson: Appier, Dcard, Coupang, Ubiquiti, OKX and Lalamove have public Greenhouse or Lever boards with Taipei roles; only Coupang had a Taipei ad that mentions dbt.

v3 (2026-10-01): 1 LinkedIn profiles taken from pages already tied to each person (event, speaker and author pages, GitHub social accounts) with research/harvest_linkedin.py, without searching. Page links are medium confidence, GitHub links high.

field_definitions.companies.job_postings.last_seen: last run in which the ad was still listed

field_definitions.companies.people.city / based_in_region: city as seen publicly; based_in_region true = evidence they are in the region, false = evidence elsewhere, null = unverified
field_definitions.companies.people.level: leadership if the title contains Head/Director/VP/Chief/Founder/C-level/Manager/Lead, otherwise working
field_definitions.companies.people.confidence: High = name + title + company visible in a public source; Medium = indirect evidence; Low = weak evidence
field_definitions.companies.people.linkedin_confidence: high = name + company/role in the search result title; medium = indirect or name variant; low = searched, not found; not_searched
field_definitions.companies.people.profile_urls: other public professional profiles, as [{type, url, source}]; meetup, x and bluesky profiles can take a message, the others show the person's work: type is one of github, meetup, zenn, qiita, velog, medium, devto, substack, ithome, sessionize, x, bluesky, website, note; source is the page that ties the profile to the person. never an email address or phone number

field_definitions.companies.people.meetup_fit.speaker_pote: high = has given a dbt talk, 2+ public talks, spoke at this chapter before, or priority_tier 1; medium = some public content; low = none found
field_definitions.companies.people.meetup_fit.attendee_pot: high = in region and public dbt content (or confirmed practitioner at a strong-dbt company); medium = in-region/unknown data practitioner; low = outside the region or weak identification
field_definitions.companies.people.internal_vinted: true for Vinted colleagues (kept for completeness, not outreach targets)
field_definitions.companies.people.priority_tier: 1 = strong recent lead: a proven speaker with a relevant recent talk, or an emerging_voice in (or not known to be outside) the region with authored content from 2024 onwards; 2 = good lead / needs verification / older content / relevant talk at another meetup; 3 = peripheral, off-topic or remote; organiser / backup / connector = special roles
field_definitions.companies.people.past_chapter_talks: talks this person gave at this chapter's own meetups, matched by name
field_definitions.companies.people.speaker_evidence.type: talk | panel | podcast | article | case_study | oss | interview | organiser | host | post | profile
field_definitions.companies.people.speaker_evidence.topics: 1-3 topics, most relevant first, only from metadata.topic_vocabulary (pipeline/enrich.py::TOPIC_VOCABULARY); organiser/host/profile entries are tagged 'community'
field_definitions.companies.people.speaker_evidence.conten: stable id; an item with several authors appears under each of them with the same content_id
field_definitions.companies.people.speaker_evidence.url_pr: direct = the item itself; overview_page = a listing/homepage where the item appears
field_definitions.past_meetups.talks.topics: 1-3 topics, most relevant first, only from metadata.topic_vocabulary (pipeline/enrich.py::TOPIC_VOCABULARY); organiser/host/profile entries are tagged 'community'
field_definitions.companies.people.lead_type: proven_speaker = has given a talk, panel or podcast, or spoke at this chapter; emerging_voice = has authored public content (blog post, article, newsletter, open-source project, LinkedIn post) but no talk found yet — a priority for first-time speaker invitations; featured = only quoted or profiled in someone else's content (case study, interview, team feature); no_public_content = none found
field_definitions.companies.people.pronouns: pronouns exactly as the person publishes them (e.g. on a speaker listing, bio or profile headline); null when not self-stated. Never inferred from names, photos or third-person wording
field_definitions.companies.people.sourced_via: channels through which the person was found (list): company_blog_scan | case_study | conference_or_meetup_agenda | data_berlin_meetup | women_in_data_community | chapter_meetup_history | newsletter_or_blog | podcast | github | linkedin_search | job_ad_company_search | other

caveats: Titles, employers and cities come from public pages and posts and may be out of date; verify before outreach.
Most iThome authors publish under a handle and do not state an employer; they sit under 'Employer not identified' and their location is unknown, although the platform is Taiwanese.
Job ads could not be read (Cloudflare). The two Yourator ads come from a fuzzy site search and do not prove dbt use.

Several chapter speakers are listed by first name only (Sam at Dcard, Joshua, Edison, Stephen, Ellen) or by Chinese name only; the assembler cannot match these, so check the past-speaker list before treating a lead as new.
The tier rule raises every emerging voice with 2024+ writing to tier 1, including authors whose posts touch dbt only lightly; read the suggested talk angle before outreach.

LinkedIn: 1 of 69 people have a profile url, taken word for word from search results. 68 were never searched (linkedin_confidence 'not_searched'); the 2026-10-01 pass searched the best-ranked leads with no known location first.
Speakers from women-in-data community events are recorded by where they spoke (sourced_via women_in_data_community). No one's gender is recorded or inferred.
WiDS Taipei 2024 speakers are listed without talk titles; their evidence links to the overview page.
Employers and dbt wording come from public job ads on 2026-10-01; ads close, so check the employer before outreach.
